observations.reading: Right page, folio 19; ka ya sta medicinal plant with Sanskrit equivalent; ka yaṅ rtse highest; ka yig letter ka; ka ye cross-reference. Full gutter text visible.

Left page, folio 18. kā tsa lin da soft cloth continues into right column; ka tsi li ban place; ka rtsam oats; ka rtsal monastery; ka rtsom alphabetic poem. ka tshal and ka dzi li ban headings occur on the facing printed page 19. HTML karma śataṃ differs from printed karma śatam.

mdun khur divination continues into right column; mdun gros plan; mdun cog table; mdun du ñe bar gnas assist; mdun du lta look; mdun du bdar cross-reference; mdun du bsdogs pa prepared continues. rkya is a quotation, phyag rten a synonym, neither an independent heading here.
ma skyes pa epithet of Brahman; ma kha ma ti Mohammed; ma mkhal cross-reference. Upper left continues ma skyes dgra; line 29 continuation is not a new heading.

ba glaṅ cross-reference; ba glaṅ rdzas utpala plant; ba rgya can spider; ba lci cow dung; ba ’jo mkhan cow milker; ba gñis pa two-sided. ba yig cin occurs as alternative under ba gcin; its independent reference is on page 8, not here.

mda’ doṅ quiver; mda’ snun byed bow; mda’ ’phen bow; mda’ ’phoṅ rwa archery ground; mda’ bo che javelin. dbu rgyan occurs in citation, nu ma ba in definition, ’phoṅ inside compound: these are not the proposed independent articles.

ba rdzi herdsman; ba yar cow calved last year; bā yi mchog sbyin Godāvarī; ba yi dug plant; ba ra dhva dza cross-reference (HTML dhwa differs); ba ra na ga coral. Printed folio and full margins visible.

Explicit ⁵ma lower thing; ma kī goddess, Sanskrit Māmakī; ma ku ra mirror; ma ke na cross-reference; ma klas contempt; ma skyes dgra Ajātaśatru continues. ma bi is a reference under ⁵ma, mā ma kī part of ma kī evidence, not separate headings.

Left printed page 16, two complete columns, folio and gutter retained. Independently visible headings: ka ma la gar bha (Madhyamaka teacher; kamalagarbha), ka ma la go mi (learned monk in southern India; kamalagomin), ka ma la can (Viṣṇu’s lotus-bearing consort), ka ma la buddhi (scholar; kamalabuddhi). dbu ma’i tshul lugs occurs within the Kamalagarbha quotation, not as an article heading. No homonym numerals visible on these four headings.

Right printed page 17, full margins and folio. Actual unnumbered headings include kā ma log (A-mdo monastery), kā ma a śo ka (young Aśoka), ka mad (the thirty letters), ka mi yam (spleen), ka mi log (country), ka mig (architectural area measure), ka mu gnas (cross-reference), ka me ka me (bending here and there). Raised 1 explicitly precedes ka med; its definition continues on page 18. Parenthetical ka references beside ka mad and ka mig are not homonym numbers.

Printed folio 353, genuine single page with two columns and complete margins. Right-column actual unnumbered headings mda’ ’joms (Wolfsmilchgewächs; dur byid), mda’ rten and mda’ lto ba (bow), mda’ ltoṅ (arrow nock; alternative mda’ stoṅ), mda’ stan (bow). Separate raised 1 mda’ stoṅ is a cross-reference to mda’ ltoṅ; raised 2 mda’ stoṅ has wüste Talöffnung and Vḍk-M 114,9. These two articles must remain distinct.

Printed folio 355, genuine single page with two complete columns. Left: unnumbered mda’ sbyin dus (Herbst; ston ka’i dus), mda’ sbron (zu Hilfe rufen); separately numbered 1 mda’ mo with Pfeil, Gewehr, divination and number-five senses, and 2 mda’ mo with Taleingang. Unnumbered mda’ tshan po means Bogenschütze. Right: mda’ ’dzin means Köcher, with iṣudhi and Ak 212.88. Both proposed mda’ mo witnesses reuse QA anchor 102:23 although the scan shows two distinct headings; this binding requires correction before certification.
